key_insight: Explicit evidence-grounding constraints improved clinical alignment in LLM-generated menstrual health summaries, but made them harder to read.
clinical_relevance: Patient-facing health summaries need to preserve clinical meaning and uncertainty while remaining understandable.
method: Generated narratives from structured menstrual health monitoring records.
Combined structured evidence conditioning with retrieval-augmented generation and prompt-based constraints.
Evaluated alignment using natural language inference, atomic factuality metrics, and readability measures.
evidence_signal: Across three LLMs and 4,500 summaries, grounding improved uncertainty preservation and generally maintained or improved faithfulness when assessed against retrieved evidence, while omission effects varied by model.
watch_item: Improved alignment came with greater reading difficulty and more medical terminology, highlighting a trade-off for patient-facing use.
paper_title: From Structured Records to Patient Narratives: Preserving Clinical Alignment in LLM-Generated Health Summaries
